newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europeans say Albania mission helped stability.
newsitem.headline: Europeans say Albania mission helped stability.

text.p: Ministers from European states with troops in Albania said on Tuesday their intervention in the Balkan country had undoubtedly stabilised the situation and demonstrated Europe's growing capacity for joint military action.

"This was a pretty remarkable example of European (military) cooperation in a crisis situation," French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette told reporters at a meeting of foreign and defence ministers from 28 countries belonging to, or associated with, the Western European Union (WEU).
"Our action undoubtedly contributed to the stabilisation of the domestic situation in Albania...and will be a model for the WEU itself to react rapidly in (future) similar crises," he said.

Albania slid into chaos and lawlessness when unrest gripped the country after a string of fraudulent savings schemes collapsed in February, depriving tens of thousands of people of their life savings.

Although the contributors to the Albania peace force are linked to the WEU, the military intervention in that country did not take place under the defence group's direct command because of differences over the political goals of the mission.
Instead, it went ahead under Italian command and WEU secretary-general Jose Cutilero expressed regrets about this during the Paris meeting.

"Coalitions of the willing, such as the one assembled for this operation, should not become the norm for European military operations of this type...They undermine the credibility of our organisation by reinforcing public perceptions that WEU's capacity for action is very limited indeed," he said.
Italy has provided the largest contingent in the multinational peace force in Albania which now numbers 6,400 men, with several new contingents still expected.

Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta called for yet further resources and aid for Albania to allow the poverty-stricken country to allow the multinational force to leave as soon as possible after elections scheduled for June 29.
